lines.s10: Rockefeller Gratin: oysters baked with bacon and creamed spinach under toasted breadcrumbs, our Thanksgiving take on oysters Rockefeller.
lines.s20: Our Rockefeller Gratin takes the New Orleans classic, oysters Rockefeller, and bakes it as a gratin: oysters with smoky bacon and creamed spinach under a crisp breadcrumb crust. It is warm, rich and briny, one of the six appetizers on the Thanksgiving Day menu.
lines.s45: Oysters Rockefeller is a New Orleans classic: oysters baked under a rich green sauce. For Thanksgiving Day the kitchen turns that idea into a gratin, grah-TAN, which means baked until the top browns. The oysters go in with bacon for smoke and salt and creamed spinach for richness, and breadcrumbs on top bake into a crisp crust. So each bite has a briny oyster, creamy greens and crunch. It is one of the six appetizers on the three course Thanksgiving menu, and a warm, rich way to start. I would pour Champagne with it.

kept.a:
The Rockefeller Gratin is one of the six appetizers on the Thanksgiving Day menu, three courses for $80, served on Thanksgiving Day only.

Its parent is oysters Rockefeller, the New Orleans classic of oysters baked under a rich green sauce. Here the kitchen builds the same flavors as a gratin: oysters, bacon and creamed spinach in one dish, with breadcrumbs over the top that bake into a crisp, golden crust. Gratin is the French word for that browned top.

On the palate it is briny from the oysters, smoky and salty from the bacon, creamy from the spinach and crunchy from the crumb. It is rich, so it suits a guest who wants a warm, generous start, and it leads well into the turkey or the beef.

The sheet lists four things and no method, so learn at lineup how the oysters are cooked, how many come in a portion and what dish it is served in.

Lead with the classic and the season: guests know oysters Rockefeller, and this is the Thanksgiving Day version, baked as a gratin. Offer it to the oyster lover and to the guest who wants something warm and rich before the turkey. Say: “It’s our take on oysters Rockefeller for the holiday: oysters baked with bacon and creamed spinach under a crisp crumb.” Then offer Champagne by the glass with it, since bubbles cut the cream and the bacon.

Asked: Is this oysters Rockefeller?

Answer: It is our Thanksgiving Day take on it. The classic is oysters baked under a rich green sauce; ours is a gratin of oysters, bacon and creamed spinach under breadcrumbs.

Asked: Are the oysters raw?

Answer: No, the gratin is baked and comes to the table hot. How long it bakes and how the oysters are handled is the kitchen’s to say, so check at lineup before you promise anything more.

Asked: Does it come with the three courses?

Answer: Yes. It is one of six appetizers to choose from on the $80 Thanksgiving Day menu.

It is a Thanksgiving Day dish only: do not offer it on another night. The sheet prints no method, so do not say how the oysters are cooked or where they come from until the kitchen tells you. It is rich, so steer a guest who wants a light start to the salad or the crudo. A question about shellfish, pork or any diet goes to the kitchen before you answer. Allergens: read the service note and confirm at lineup.

value.wine: Brennan’s Essential by Piper-Heidsieck Extra Brut NV
value.why: Bubbles and acid cut cream, bacon fat and a buttery crumb, and a chalky finish suits a briny oyster.
value.sayIt: With the Rockefeller Gratin I’d pour our house Champagne: the bubbles cut the cream and bacon, and it loves an oyster.
value.whyThisWine: The gratin is rich on rich: cream, bacon and a toasted crumb over a briny oyster. Our house Champagne is very dry, so its bubbles and acidity clear the cream, and its toasty note sits with the breadcrumbs.
value.palate: The cream and the bacon coat the palate, and the Champagne’s bubbles and acidity lift them off, so the next bite tastes as bright as the first. The oyster’s brine makes the wine’s citrus seem riper, the toasted crumb picks up its brioche note, and the finish is clean and chalky rather than heavy.
value.second: Famille Durand Val de Loire Sauvignon Blanc 2025
value.secondWhy: For a guest who wants a still white: the Sauvignon Blanc is crisp and citrusy, bright enough for the cream and clean beside the oyster.
value.serve: Pour as the appetizers fire, well chilled, in a Champagne glass. Confirm at lineup that the house Champagne is poured on Thanksgiving Day.
value.avoid: Avoid tannic reds and heavily oaked whites: tannin turns metallic beside an oyster, and oak piles weight on a dish that is already rich.
value.zeroProof: Oh! What It Seemed to Be
value.zeroProofWhy: lemon and a silky texture lift the cream and the bacon without fighting the oyster.
